details: The European Central Bank's Governing Council decided on October 29, 2026, to keep its three key interest rates unchanged. This decision comes as energy prices continue to rise, posing upside risks to inflation and downside risks to economic growth. Adding to market uncertainty, ECB President Christine Lagarde announced her early departure from her post in February 2027, ahead of her term's official end. This follows a period of tightening financial conditions and eurozone inflation nearing double the ECB's 2% target.
title: ECB Holds Rates Amid Inflation, Lagarde to Depart Early

details: The Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates steady at 3.75%-4.00% on October 28, 2026, a move largely anticipated by financial markets. Despite ongoing concerns about inflation, the Fed opted for a pause. Attention now shifts to Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's upcoming statements for any indications regarding the likelihood of a rate hike in December, which many analysts consider a strong possibility.
title: Fed Keeps Rates Unchanged; Future Hike Signals Watched

details: In its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) projects global growth to decelerate to 3.1% in 2026. The report also anticipates global headline inflation to notably increase to 4.7% in 2026 before easing in 2027. The IMF highlights continued strains from geopolitical tensions, persistent energy market disruptions, and growing fiscal vulnerabilities as key risks to the economic outlook.
title: IMF Outlook: Slower Global Growth, Rising Inflation for 2026

details: Cryptocurrency exchange HTX (formerly Huobi) has agreed to stop promoting its cryptoasset services to customers in the United Kingdom. This decision follows a High Court agreement with Britain's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), which had sued HTX for unlawfully promoting crypto services. The settlement, announced on October 29, 2026, marks a significant regulatory enforcement action and requires HTX to close existing UK customer accounts.
title: HTX Crypto Exchange Exits UK After Regulator Lawsuit

details: A joint venture between Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE's owner) and crypto exchange OKX to launch tokenized versions of blue-chip US stocks has encountered significant resistance. Over half of the 62 companies initially targeted, including major tech giants like Alphabet and Microsoft, have formally objected to their shares being tokenized. Concerns raised include potential impacts on stock pricing, liquidity, volatility, and investor confusion, highlighting ongoing tensions between traditional finance and blockchain innovation.
title: Big Tech Firms Oppose NYSE Owner's Tokenized Stock Venture
